body:
DISSOLVED by §58 (T261, merged 2026-09-01, PR #517): every binding target is under a person, so every channel is in someone's reach — S5 (T266).

`loam federate open --into friends --prefix alice` (the CLI's own example) and `loam_federate_connect` both declare `into` when it is new — curated, shared, and with NO parent. The admin page's reach is `subtreeOf(table, user)`, walking parent and inboxOf edges from the container named after the session user, so such a channel's pool is outside every subtree: no dashboard panel lists it, `GET /admin/container?name=channel:friends:alice` answers notYours, and the orphaned-channels block does not apply (that block is for channels whose `into` was STRUCK, and it offers CLI verbs only). T257 made the page's plan reach channel pools and complete the sever — for channels whose `into` sits in the session user's subtree — and made `loam_federate_drop`'s reply say, for a rootless `into`, that the CLI severs it. Found by a P5 lens on T257, 2026-09-01.

The remaining question is a DECISION about the admin door's trust model (§40), so it is Myk's: (1) should an operator-ROLE session reach containers outside every subtree — making the store-wide read the operator already has (the orphan block) also a store-wide act; (2) or should `into` containers opened without a parent be declared UNDER the opener's root when the opener is a session user or a connection bound to one (§39), so the ordinary subtree reach covers them; (3) or should the page stay per-subtree and the tool keep pointing rootless channels at the CLI (the T257 state). Each is coherent; (2) is closest to §39's model; (1) is the smallest change.

Acceptance criteria (draft, settled at P1):
- (a) Whichever reach is chosen, a channel opened by the CLI's example into a fresh container is severable from the browser by the person the design names, two-sided at the bytes, or the tool's reply states truthfully that it is not. Verify: test/server/admin-channel-reach.test.ts.
- (b) A non-operator session still learns nothing about containers outside its subtree (the §40 oracle promise). Verify: the same suite.
title: A channel opened into a rootless container has no page: decide who may finish its sever in the browser
